title: landing-funnels-by-segment-copyplaybook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for segmented homepage and product landing copy experiments. Goal: find 2–3 hero + mid-funnel variants per segment that can be A/B tested and instrumented into the site for Q2 trial. Not a finalized messaging doc — intentionally rough, prioritizes speed and testability.

Context and constraints:
- Audience: engineering-first buyers (developers, ML engineers), platform teams (SRE/infra), and procurement/IT for enterprise deals.
- Primary positioning anchor: inference as a production problem (latency, cost, reliability, deploy flexibility). Avoid generic "AI model" fluff.
- Tone: technical but accessible. Developer voice (concise, measurable claims) for dev audience; trust-forward and risk-aware for enterprise landing paths.
- Measurements: primary metric = signups-from-trial-CTA; secondary = demo-requests and pricing-page visits. Add instrumentation tags to each CTA.

Segments and high-level funnels (for split tests):
1) Developer/Startup funnel (self-serve, quick time-to-value)
   - Entry hook: low friction, quick integration, free credits
   - Primary hero claim: "Get production-grade LLM inference in minutes — no infra to manage."
   - Mid-funnel nudges: SDK examples (JS/Python), quickstart repo link, latency/cost snapshot for common use cases
   - CTA hierarchy: Start free -> Read quickstart -> Repo
   - Risk messaging: "Pay-as-you-go, cancel anytime; community and docs support."

2) Platform/Infra funnel (platform teams, internal infra owners)
   - Entry hook: predictable capacity, autoscaling control, routing policies
   - Primary hero claim: "Unify inference across environments — same API, consistent SLOs."
   - Mid-funnel: Dedicated capacity microcopy (commits, burst), SDK/infra integration notes (Kubernetes, Terraform examples)
   - CTA: Request capacity quote -> View capacity calculator -> Technical docs

3) Enterprise/Regulated funnel (security, compliance, on-prem)
   - Entry hook: private deployments, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2/SLA
   - Primary hero claim: "Run LLM inference inside your VPC or on-prem with enterprise controls."
   - Mid-funnel: Compliance checklist, architecture diagram, reference customers (anonymized), legal/contract path
   - CTA: Contact sales -> Download compliance brief -> Request architecture review

Hero copy variants (shortlisted, each in three tones: direct, engineering, enterprise-trust):
A1 (Direct): "Make inference predictable. Ship features faster."
A2 (Engineering): "Low-latency, high-throughput LLM inference—tuned for production workloads."
A3 (Enterprise): "Secure, SLA-backed LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Subhead options (supporting claims):
- "Unified API for hosted, reserved, and private deployments — same SDK, same contract."
- "Optimize latency and cost with intelligent batching, caching, and model routing."
- "SLA-backed uptime, audit logs, and customer-managed keys for regulated workloads."

Microcopy and trust signals (to use across variants):
- Small-badge style: "Verified performance profiles" | "SLA: 99.9%" | "SOC2-ready"
- Per-CTA microcopy: "Start free — includes $200 credit" | "Request a dedicated capacity estimate" | "Talk to an engineer"
- Inline metric snippets: "Typical 75ms median completion for 512-token Llama-variant" (only use after verification).

Product-page headline + subcopy sketches (three product verticals):
1) Redwood API (hosted)
   - Headline: "Hosted inference with instant scale and predictable SLAs"
   - Bullets: "REST & SDKs, streaming, tool/function calling, usage analytics"; "Free tier + pay-as-you-go"
   - CTA: "Create API key"

2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - Headline: "Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation"
   - Bullets: "Configurable autoscaling, burst capacity, per-tenant quotas"; "Monthly commits with cost predictability"
   - CTA: "Estimate capacity"

3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Headline: "Air-gapped or VPC deployments with enterprise controls"
   - Bullets: "Customer-managed keys, private control plane, on-prem package"; "Integrations: Okta, Azure AD, HashiCorp Vault"
   - CTA: "Request a private deployment brief"

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Variant axis 1: Audience segment (developer, platform, enterprise)
- Variant axis 2: Claim emphasis (latency/cost control vs. deployment flexibility vs. security/trust)
- Variant axis 3: CTA funnel (self-serve credits vs. demo vs. quote)
- N: Run 6-week tests per segment, stop early on +10% primary conversion lift or clear negative signal.

Competitive notes (concise, blunt):
- Cloud-managed AI endpoints: usually high convenience but variable latency and pricing unpredictability at scale. Use as negative anchor for Dedicated messaging (predictable throughput).
- LLM API startups: strong on simplicity — beat them on developer ergonomics (quickstart, SDKs, microbenchmarks) and on cost controls (batching, quantization advice).
- Open-source runtimes/self-host: lower unit cost potential but high ops burden. Lead with "same API, less ops" — emphasize rollouts + fallback policies as value.

Objections & short rebuttals (for microcopy / sales scripts):
- "We can run models ourselves cheaper." -> "Maybe — but we charge for predictability and fewer engineering hours. Many customers reduce TCO after accounting for SRE + infra ops."
- "Is latency really better?" -> "Show a latency profile for your sample workload—our benchmark settings are reproducible; we recommend a test route with your prompt set."
- "How do we keep data private?" -> "Private deployment & VPC options plus KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we can run an on-prem proof-of-concept."

Bundle copy for experiments (full hero examples):
Variant X (developer-first):
Headline: "Ship LLM features without building an infra team"
Subhead: "Start with the hosted API, scale to Dedicated when you need throughput. JS/Python SDKs, free credits to try."
Primary CTA: "Start free"  Secondary: "See quickstart"

Variant Y (platform-first):
Headline: "Predictable inference at scale for platform teams"
Subhead: "Dedicated pools, autoscaling policies, and routing rules — keep SLOs tight and costs measurable."
Primary CTA: "Estimate capacity" Secondary: "View integration guide"

Variant Z (enterprise trust):
Headline: "Secure LLM serving with enterprise controls and SLAs"
Subhead: "Private control plane, end-to-end audit trails, and customer-managed keys."
Primary CTA: "Request a compliance brief" Secondary: "Talk to sales"

Measurements & instrumentation checklist (to hand to web dev/analytics):
- UTM and experiment id on each CTA
- Event: hero_cta_click (label: variant, segment)
- Funnel step events: quickstart_started, api_key_created, demo_requested, capacity_quote_requested
- Attach cost-per-acquisition and LTV back to Salesforce lead records for long-run evaluation

Open questions / notes to resolve before bake:
- Verify latency and cost snippets with Applied ML (Diego) and Infra (Ethan) — avoid publishing numbers without verification.
- Add 1–2 reference customer blurbs for Dedicated and Private pages; legal to approve disclaimers.
- Decide if free credits are advertised site-wide or gated behind signup funnel (privacy/abuse tradeoff).

Next steps (owner: Maya):
1) Run quick hallway tests with developer docs preview (staging) — gather qualitative feedback by 2026-03-05.
2) Lock 3 hero variants (one per segment) and create A/B experiments with analytics tags by 2026-03-18.
3) Coordinate with Applied ML for metric verification and Solutions Eng for sales snippets.

Slack refs and recent threads: #gtm-copy -> thread: "landing funnels Q2" (see slack/threads/GTMCOPY-landing-2026)
Jira tickets to create: RDW-PRIOR-landing-experiments, RDW-PRIOR-copy-audit

Notes (informal):
- Avoid generic "AI that does X" lines. Engineers care about reproducible claims and examples.
- Keep hero copy short; use mid-funnel space for nuance.
- If stuck: default to the developer-first variant for the header with an enterprise-focused subnav for regulated buyers.
